title: Criticality, Gaussian fields and exact block renormalization

items.title: Infinite-volume nonanalytic-pressure criticality
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of values of a scalar control parameter $\theta$, expressed in one fixed unit if it is dimensional. Let $(N_n)_{n\ge1}$ be positive integers with $N_n\to\infty$, interpreted as finite system sizes such as site counts. A finite-volume partition-function sequence on $I$ is a sequence of real-analytic functions $Z_n:I\to(0,\infty)$. For each $n$, define its dimensionless log partition density per site by $p_n(\theta):=N_n^{-1}\log Z_n(\theta)$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. If the pointwise limit $p(\theta):=\lim_{n\to\infty}p_n(\theta)$ exists as a finite real number for every $\theta\in I$, call $p$ the infinite-volume pressure associated with this sequence. A point $\theta_c\in I$ is critical under the nonanalytic-pressure criterion exactly when there do not exist $\epsilon>0$ with $(\theta_c-\epsilon,\theta_c+\epsilon)\subseteq I$ and real coefficients $(a_k)_{k\ge0}$ such that $p(\theta)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k(\theta-\theta_c)^k$ throughout that interval. Finite-volume analyticity and a finite-size maximum of a derivative do not, by themselves, establish criticality under this definition.

This is one precise thermodynamic criticality criterion; it makes no claim that a particular interacting model satisfies it. A divergent correlation length is a separate criterion and is not identified with pressure nonanalyticity without an additional theorem.

items.title: Finite Gaussian probability with a positive precision matrix
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice: every sequence $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of nonempty sets has a function $f$ with $f(n)\in X_n$ for every $n$. For $N\ge1$, a real symmetric positive-definite matrix $K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ (meaning $z^{\mathsf T}Kz>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^N$) defines the finite centered Gaussian probability $\gamma_K$ on $\mathbb R^N$ by

$$Z_K:=\int_{\mathbb R^N}e^{-z^{\mathsf T}Kz/2}\,d\lambda_N(z),\qquad \gamma_K(dz):=Z_K^{-1}e^{-z^{\mathsf T}Kz/2}\,d\lambda_N(z).$$

Under the stated Axiom of Countable Choice, $Z_K=(2\pi)^{N/2}(\det K)^{-1/2}$, $\mathbb E_{\gamma_K}[z]=0$, and $\operatorname{Cov}_{\gamma_K}(z)=K^{-1}$; these identities are the positive-quadratic-form Gaussian theorem of the mathematical supplier. Here $K$ is called the precision matrix because it appears in the quadratic exponent, and the covariance is its inverse. For $N=0$, define $\mathbb R^0$ to be the singleton containing the empty vector and define $\gamma_{\varnothing}$ to put mass one on that point; its partition factor and empty determinant are both $1$.

The variables $z_i$ and exponent $z^{\mathsf T}Kz/2$ are dimensionless in this mathematical definition. In a physical quadratic model, if $\Phi_i$ has field unit $\Phi_*$ and $H(\Phi)=\frac12\Phi^{\mathsf T}K_{\rm phys}\Phi$, then each entry of $K_{\rm phys}$ has units $\mathrm J/(\Phi_*)^2$. With $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ and $z_i=\Phi_i/\Phi_*$, the dimensionless precision is $K=\beta\Phi_*^2K_{\rm phys}$. This dimensional conversion does not assert an empirical model.

items.title: Fourier spectrum and positivity of the periodic lattice Laplacian
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and $L\ge1$ be integers, let $\Lambda_{d,L}:=(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$, and represent every residue coordinate by its unique value in $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Write $e_j$ for the $j$th coordinate class, and count the two terms $x+e_j$ and $x-e_j$ separately even when they coincide for $L=1$ or $L=2$. For a real function $f$ on $\Lambda_{d,L}$, define

$$(-\Delta f)(x):=\sum_{j=1}^d\bigl(2f(x)-f(x+e_j)-f(x-e_j)\bigr).$$

Extend $-\Delta$ complex-linearly. For $r=(r_1,\ldots,r_d)\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d$, define $\chi_r(x):=\exp(2\pi i\,r\cdot x/L)$. With inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=L^{-d}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_{d,L}}f(x)\overline{g(x)}$, the $L^d$ characters $\chi_r$ form an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb C^{\Lambda_{d,L}}$ and satisfy

$$-\Delta\chi_r=\lambda_r\chi_r,\qquad \lambda_r=4\sum_{j=1}^d\sin^2(\pi r_j/L).$$

Consequently $-\Delta$ is real symmetric positive semidefinite, and for $m^2>0$ and $\kappa>0$ the matrix $m^2I_{\Lambda_{d,L}}+\kappa(-\Delta)$ is real symmetric positive definite with eigenvalues $m^2+4\kappa\sum_j\sin^2(\pi r_j/L)>0$.

items.title: Chord and Lipschitz bounds for sine
items.statement: For $|u|\le\pi/2$, $2|u|/\pi\le|\sin u|\le|u|$. For all real $u,v$, $|\sin u-\sin v|\le|u-v|$.

items.title: Positive Schur complements for finite Gaussian precisions
items.statement:
Let $r\ge0$ and $s\ge1$ be integers, and let

$$K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{(r+s)\times(r+s)}$$

be symmetric positive definite, with $A\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}$ and $C\in\mathbb R^{s\times s}$. Then $C$ is symmetric positive definite, $\det C>0$, and $C^{-1}$ exists. The Schur complement $S:=A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}$ is symmetric positive definite when $r\ge1$; when $r=0$, $S$ is the empty $0\times0$ matrix. For all $x\in\mathbb R^r$ and $y\in\mathbb R^s$,

$$\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}^{\mathsf T}K\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=x^{\mathsf T}Sx+(y+C^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}x)^{\mathsf T}C(y+C^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}x).$$

For $r=0$, the first term and $S$ are interpreted on the singleton space $\mathbb R^0$.

items.title: Unconstrained massless periodic Gaussian has infinite normalizer
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $d,L\ge1$ be integers, let $\Lambda_{d,L}=(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$ have $N=L^d$ sites, and let $\kappa>0$. Define the zero-mass precision $K:=\kappa(-\Delta)$ on $\mathbb R^{\Lambda_{d,L}}$, with the periodic Laplacian convention of [[lem-csm-frontier-periodic-laplacian-spectrum]]. Then the unrestricted Lebesgue normalizer diverges:

$$\int_{\mathbb R^{\Lambda_{d,L}}}\exp\!\left(-\frac12z^{\mathsf T}Kz\right)\,d\lambda_N(z)=+\infty.$$

Thus this quadratic weight does not define a probability density on the full coordinate space. A finite-volume massless Gaussian must first restrict the field, for example to $\{z:\sum_{x\in\Lambda_{d,L}}z_x=0\}$, before inverting the Laplacian.

items.title: Finite periodic Gaussian lattice field with positive mass
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice from [[def-countable-choice]]. Let integers $d,L\ge1$ specify the periodic lattice $\Lambda_{d,L}=(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$ and let $m^2>0$ and $\kappa>0$ be dimensionless real parameters in lattice units. On the real coordinate space $\mathbb R^{\Lambda_{d,L}}$, let

$$K_{d,L,m,\kappa}:=m^2I+\kappa(-\Delta),$$

where $-\Delta$ is the periodic Laplacian of [[lem-csm-frontier-periodic-laplacian-spectrum]]. Its eigenvalues are

$$m^2+4\kappa\sum_{j=1}^d\sin^2(\pi r_j/L),\qquad r\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^d,$$

so it is symmetric positive definite. The finite periodic Gaussian lattice field is the centered probability $\gamma_{K_{d,L,m,\kappa}}$ of [[def-csm-frontier-finite-gaussian-precision]], with density proportional to $\exp(-z^{\mathsf T}K_{d,L,m,\kappa}z/2)$ against Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^{L^d}$ and covariance $K_{d,L,m,\kappa}^{-1}$ by [[thm-csm-examples-quadratic-covariance]] at $\beta=1$.

The lattice coordinates $z_x$ and the quadratic exponent are dimensionless. A physical model may set $z_x=\Phi_x/\Phi_*$ and divide its energy by $k_BT$, where $\Phi_*$ is a declared field unit and $T>0$ is temperature; this definition itself makes no empirical claim. At $m^2=0$, the constant field is a zero mode and the unrestricted normalizer diverges by [[lem-csm-frontier-massless-torus-normalization-diverges]], so the full-space positive-precision definition does not apply. A finite-volume massless model must first specify a restriction such as the subspace $\sum_{x\in\Lambda_{d,L}}z_x=0$ before inverting the Laplacian.

items.title: Dimension threshold for the infinite-lattice massless Gaussian Green integral
items.statement:
For integer $d\ge1$, coupling $\kappa>0$, and $k=(k_1,\ldots,k_d)\in[-\pi,\pi]^d$, put

$$D_d(k):=4\sum_{j=1}^d\sin^2(k_j/2).$$

For $x\in\mathbb Z^d$, define the massless infinite-lattice Green integral when it is finite by

$$G_{d,\kappa}(x):=(2\pi)^{-d}\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^d}\frac{\cos(k\cdot x)}{\kappa D_d(k)}\,d\lambda_d(k),$$

where the integrand is assigned value $0$ at $k=0$, which does not affect the Lebesgue integral. If $d>2$, this integral is absolutely finite for every fixed $x\in\mathbb Z^d$. If $1\le d\le2$, the diagonal integral with $x=0$ is $+\infty$. Thus the dimension threshold concerns this free Gaussian Fourier integral; it does not assert an interacting critical exponent or a continuum scaling limit.

items.title: Exact finite Gaussian block elimination
items.statement:
The exact Gaussian block-elimination algorithm has input:

- an integer $N\ge1$ and a real symmetric positive-definite precision matrix $K_0\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$;
- an integer $q\ge0$ and nested retained coordinate sets
  $$R_0=\{1,\ldots,N\}\supseteq R_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq R_q,$$
  each given in increasing coordinate order.

It starts at stage $0$ with the ordered coordinates $R_0$ and matrix $K_0$. For each $j=1,\ldots,q$, let $E_j=R_{j-1}\setminus R_j$ be the coordinates to eliminate at that stage.

1. If $E_j=\varnothing$, set $K_j=K_{j-1}$ and $\ell_j=0$.
2. If $E_j\ne\varnothing$, reorder the current coordinates as $R_j$ followed by $E_j$ and write the correspondingly permuted matrix
   $$K_{j-1}=\begin{pmatrix}A_j&B_j\\B_j^{\mathsf T}&C_j\end{pmatrix}.$$
   Solve the nonsingular system $C_jX_j=B_j^{\mathsf T}$, set
   $$K_j:=A_j-B_jX_j,\qquad \ell_j:=\frac{|E_j|}{2}\ln(2\pi)-\frac12\ln(\det C_j).$$

The output is $(K_q,\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_q)$, with the accumulated log normalization $\sum_{j=1}^q\ell_j$. When $R_j=\varnothing$, $K_j$ is the unique empty $0\times0$ matrix and its determinant is defined to be $1$. This is an exact-arithmetic procedure on finite matrices. When $K_0$ is a precision of [[def-csm-frontier-gaussian-lattice]], the log increments are intended to record the normalization changes from eliminating the stated coordinates; a separate correctness theorem proves that finite-dimensional Gaussian identity.

items.title: Correctness of finite Gaussian block elimination
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and the hypotheses of [[alg-csm-frontier-gaussian-block-rg]] with input $K_0$ and retained sets $R_0,\ldots,R_q$. Let $K_j,C_j,\ell_j$ be the algorithm outputs. At each stage write $E_j=R_{j-1}\setminus R_j$, and use the empty-set conventions of the algorithm. Then the algorithm terminates after $q$ stages, every nonempty retained precision $K_j$ is positive definite, and for every fixed retained vector $x\in\mathbb R^{R_q}$,

$$\int_{\mathbb R^{\bigcup_{j=1}^q E_j}}\exp\!\left(-\frac12 \widetilde z(x,y)^{\mathsf T}K_0\widetilde z(x,y)\right)\,d\lambda(y) =\exp\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^q\ell_j\right)\exp\!\left(-\frac12x^{\mathsf T}K_qx\right),$$

where $y$ lists the eliminated coordinates in increasing order, $\widetilde z(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{R_0}$ is the unique full coordinate vector agreeing with $x$ on $R_q$ and with $y$ on $R_0\setminus R_q$, and $\lambda$ is Euclidean Lebesgue measure in that finite-dimensional space. If $R_q\ne\varnothing$, the normalized marginal law of the retained coordinates under $\gamma_{K_0}$ is exactly $\gamma_{K_q}$; if $R_q=\varnothing$, the final retained space is the singleton $\mathbb R^0$ and the identity gives $Z_{K_0}=\exp(\sum_j\ell_j)$. In all cases,

$$\ln Z_{K_0}=\sum_{j=1}^q\ell_j+\ln Z_{K_q},$$

with $Z_{K_q}=1$ under the empty-space convention. These are exact finite-dimensional Gaussian identities and make no approximation or empirical claim.

items.title: Engineering scaling of the Gaussian gradient and quartic actions
items.statement:
Let integer $d\ge1$, dimensionless scale factor $b>0$, and real smooth compactly supported field $\varphi'\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ be given. Define

$$\varphi_b(x):=b^{-(d-2)/2}\varphi'(x/b),\qquad x\in\mathbb R^d.$$

For a real smooth compactly supported field $\psi$, define its Gaussian gradient action and quartic integral by

$$S_2[\psi]:=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\nabla\psi(x)|^2\,d\lambda_d(x),\qquad Q_4[\psi]:=\frac1{4!}\int_{\mathbb R^d}\psi(x)^4\,d\lambda_d(x),$$

where $\nabla$ is the vector of first partial derivatives. Then

$$S_2[\varphi_b]=S_2[\varphi'],\qquad Q_4[\varphi_b]=b^{4-d}Q_4[\varphi'].$$

Consequently a coefficient $g$ multiplying $Q_4$ transforms to $g'=b^{4-d}g$ when the action is re-expressed in the rescaled coordinate $x'=x/b$. This is engineering power counting on smooth test fields; it neither constructs an interacting probability measure nor proves an interacting critical exponent.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Field Theory, complete Cambridge lecture notes
references.locator: §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 59–69 / PDF pp. 63–73, Gaussian scaling dimensions and engineering power counting.

title: Criticality, Gaussian fields and exact block renormalization — Examples

items.title: Exact elimination of a Gaussian star generates pair couplings
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let integer $n\ge2$. Let $\mathbf1_n\in\mathbb R^n$ have every coordinate equal to $1$, and define the precision matrix on $n$ leaf variables and one central variable by

$$K_n:=\begin{pmatrix}2nI_n&\mathbf1_n\\\mathbf1_n^{\mathsf T}&1\end{pmatrix}.$$

This matrix is positive definite, so it defines a finite centered Gaussian law with precision $K_n$. Its leaf-to-leaf precision entries are initially zero for distinct leaves. Eliminating the central coordinate exactly gives leaf precision

$$K_{\mathrm{leaf}}=2nI_n-\mathbf1_n\mathbf1_n^{\mathsf T},$$

whose off-diagonal entry is $-1$ for every pair of distinct leaves. Thus one exact Gaussian block step creates a nonzero pair interaction between every two leaves, even though those pairs had no direct precision entry in the original star.
